my_own_diagnosis: The bottom-up progression from oldest/lowest leaves upward while new growth stays green is the textbook signature of a mobile-nutrient deficiency — nitrogen being the primary candidate in a fruiting container tomato with depleted potting mix; I would reject the iron/pH lockout hypothesis because iron is immobile and always presents first on young upper tissue.
focal_notes: The ascending progression pattern from oldest to newest leaves is a well-established differential that unambiguously points to mobile-nutrient (nitrogen) deficiency and structurally excludes the iron-lockout distractor.
oracle_notes: HL/LL cell oracles correctly map to the low-diagnostic oracle (withhold nitrogen diagnosis, ask about feeding/potting mix), and HH/LH correctly map to the focal oracle (confirm nitrogen, exclude iron/pH); low_diagnostic_oracle_focus properly withholds the distractor diagnosis.
